analysis.one_liner: L&T is India's largest engineering, construction and infrastructure conglomerate, executing large domestic and international EPC projects (power, hydrocarbons, infrastructure) alongside manufacturing and technology services run through subsidiaries.
analysis.whats_happening: L&T reported Q2 FY27 results (quarter to September 2026) on 27 October 2026 — just three days before the last price used here. Revenue rose 16% YoY to ₹78,750 crore and net profit rose 33% to ₹5,202 crore, on the back of a record quarterly order inflow of ₹1,47,665 crore (up 28% YoY), taking the order book to ₹8.53 lakh crore. Recent order wins in October included large power transmission contracts in Saudi Arabia and the UAE and metro-rail work in Dhaka. Alongside this, the board is moving L&T's Realty business into a wholly-owned subsidiary via a court-approved scheme — this is an internal reorganisation, not a spin-off distributed to shareholders.
analysis.plain_terms: Business is growing fast on paper: more orders coming in, more revenue booked, more profit earned. The tension is that profit margins are shrinking even as revenue grows — operating margin fell from about 10% to 8.7% year-on-year, and management itself has guided to a lower full-year margin target (7.8%) than the company has historically run at. So this is a case of strong volume growth masking a genuine, management-acknowledged erosion in how much of each rupee of work actually turns into profit, mainly because more of the order book is now in lower-margin manufacturing/product work and because some infrastructure projects are running into cost overruns.
analysis.quarters: Q1 FY27 (June 2026 quarter): revenue ₹67,942 crore (+7% YoY), PAT ₹4,123 crore (+14%), EBITDA margin 9.0% (down from 9.9%), order inflow ₹1.08 lakh crore. Q2 FY27 (Sept 2026 quarter): revenue ₹78,750 crore (+16%), PAT ₹5,202 crore (+33%), EBITDA margin down further to 8.7% from 10.0% a year earlier. Management explicitly attributed the margin decline to 'lower margin across portfolio and change in revenue mix' — a higher share of lower-margin Projects/Products/Manufacturing (PPM) work. Within segments, Infrastructure & Utilities margin fell to 5.7% from 6.2% on cost pressure in water/effluent-treatment projects, while Manufacturing & Products was a bright spot, with revenue up 34% and margin up 220 basis points to 15.7%. Management reiterated FY27 guidance of 10-12% growth in both order inflow and revenue, alongside a full-year EBITDA margin target of 7.8% — itself a step down from prior years, and worth tracking for whether it marks a floor or a continuing slide. One source showed a conflicting PAT figure of ₹5,949 crore for the quarter; this is an outlier against 8+ other sources agreeing on ₹5,202 crore, so the latter is used here.
analysis.performance_read: Over 1 year the stock is down 1.96%, which is actually better than the Nifty (-10.92%) but well behind peer Siemens (+6.15%). Over 3 years L&T is up 35.78% versus the Nifty's 20.83% but has badly lagged Siemens' 71.03%. Over 5 years the gap is similar: L&T +126.91% against Nifty +28.58% and Siemens +157.80%. The stock is currently 11.5% below its February 2026 peak of ₹4,375 — a modest pullback, not a crash, and there is no recent demerger or spin-off in L&T's own history (the Realty transfer stays inside a wholly-owned subsidiary, so nothing is being distributed to shareholders) that would understate these returns. The company's older stock splits (2004-2017) predate this return window and are standard adjustments already reflected in the price series. The honest read: L&T has been a steady, market-beating performer in absolute terms but a persistent laggard against its closest listed peer across every horizon shown.
analysis.valuation_read: The stock trades around 28-30x trailing earnings (sources showed a modest spread) with a dividend yield of under 1%. This is not a cheap stock by headline multiple. Why it carries this multiple: a record and diversified order book (54% international), a reputation as India's bellwether capital-goods/infrastructure executor, and no promoter overhang. Whether that premium is justified is a separate question — it is being paid for at the same time management is guiding margins lower, which is an unusual combination; a premium multiple alongside shrinking margins only makes sense if investors believe current margin pressure is temporary mix-shift rather than a structural reset. Price-to-book and ROCE figures showed meaningful disagreement across sources during this review (P/B estimates ranged roughly 4.6x-6.5x, ROCE 14.6%-19%) — treat any single number with caution; check Screener directly for the current figure.
analysis.growth_read: Growth here is primarily volume-led: revenue is up double digits and the order book hit a record, driven by genuinely higher order wins and execution rather than price increases. But it is not margin-led growth — in fact margins are moving the wrong way, down from 10.0% to 8.7% EBITDA margin year-on-year, explicitly because the revenue mix has shifted toward lower-margin manufacturing/products work and because some infrastructure segments are absorbing cost overruns. For a project-execution business, volume growth with falling margins is the less durable combination than growth in both — it means L&T is working harder for a smaller slice of each rupee.
analysis.health_read: Net debt-to-equity reportedly improved to about 0.38 from 0.62 over the past year, and net working capital improved to 4.9% of revenue from 10.1% — both encouraging signs that profits are converting into cash rather than sitting in receivables or inventory, though these specific debt figures come from a single source and were not independently cross-verified; treat as moderate confidence. ROE is around 15-16%. For a company of L&T's scale and project-based model, the more relevant risk is business risk (project execution, margin mix, cost overruns on fixed-price contracts) rather than financial risk — leverage looks manageable and is trending down.
analysis.ownership_read: L&T has no promoter in the conventional Indian sense — it is institutionally owned and professionally managed, with 0% classified as promoter holding. This is a structural feature of the company, not a governance gap, and it also means pledging is not applicable (there is no promoter entity to pledge shares). The largest single shareholder is LIC at roughly 12.51%, with FIIs holding about 19.2% and domestic institutions (mutual funds, insurers) around 42.9% combined. No single marquee retail-style investor is on the register beyond these institutional holders.
strengths: Record quarterly order inflow of ₹1,47,665 crore in Q2 FY27 (+28% YoY), taking the order book to ₹8.53 lakh crore, 54% of it international
Revenue and profit both growing strongly: Q2 FY27 revenue +16% YoY to ₹78,750 crore, PAT +33% to ₹5,202 crore
Working capital discipline improving — net working capital down to 4.9% of revenue from 10.1% a year earlier, alongside falling net debt-to-equity
Manufacturing & Products segment outperforming, with revenue up 34% and margin up 220 basis points to 15.7%, showing the group has pockets of improving profitability even as the overall mix dilutes
watchpoints: EBITDA margin has fallen from 10.0% to 8.7% YoY, and management's own FY27 target of 7.8% is itself a step down from historical levels
Infrastructure & Utilities segment margin slipped to 5.7% from 6.2% on cost pressure in water/effluent-treatment projects — a sign of execution risk on fixed-price contracts
Stock has meaningfully underperformed peer Siemens over 3 years (+35.8% vs +71.0%) and 5 years (+126.9% vs +157.8%), despite beating the Nifty
Trading at roughly 28-30x trailing earnings with under 1% dividend yield while guiding to lower margins — a premium multiple that assumes the margin pressure is temporary
analysis.one_thing: Whether the Q3 FY27 print (expected around late January 2027, date not yet confirmed) shows EBITDA margin stabilising near management's 7.8% guided target or continuing to slide — that will show whether the current margin compression is a one-off mix shift or a structural reset in profitability.
analysis.data_notes: Q2 FY27 revenue, PAT and order inflow figures were cross-checked across 8+ independent financial news sources and are consistent (₹78,750 cr revenue, ₹5,202 cr PAT, ₹1,47,665 cr order inflow); one outlier source (₹5,949 cr PAT) was set aside as inconsistent with the broader cluster. P/B and ROCE figures showed real disagreement across sources (P/B roughly 4.6x-6.5x, ROCE 14.6%-19%) and could not be reconciled here — not verified, check Screener directly. Net debt-to-equity and gross debt-to-equity figures came from a single source and are moderate-confidence only. The next results date (Q3 FY27) is an estimate based on historical timing, not a confirmed date. A reported FY27 interim dividend record date may have been conflated with a separate dividend declared by listed subsidiary L&T Technology Services rather than the parent — not included in this report pending direct confirmation.
